facts.statement: The first Incisivosaurus specimen, a skull named IVPP V13326, was described by Xu et al. in 2002 from the Barremian stage of the Yixian Formation in western Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: The first specimen to be described (by Xu et al. in 2002), IVPP V13326, is a skull that was collected from the lowermost levels (the fluvial Lujiatun beds) of the Yixian Formation (dating to the Barremian stage about 126 million years ago) in the Sihetun area, near Beipiao City, in western Liaoning Province.

facts.statement: The genus name Incisivosaurus refers to the dinosaur's prominent, rodent-like front teeth that show wear patterns typical of plant-eaters.
facts.quote: It was named for its prominent, rodent-like front teeth, which show wear patterns commonly found in plant-eating dinosaurs.

facts.statement: A 2004 study described Incisivosaurus as having a long snout comprising about half the skull length, a slender lower jaw with a long opening, and distinctive large, flattened front teeth.
facts.quote: A subsequent study by Osmolska et al. in 2004 described the distinguishing skeletal features of Incisivosaurus, including a long snout that made up about half the total length of the skull, a slender lower jaw with a long fenestra (opening), and its distinctive, large, flattened front teeth.

facts.statement: In an unweighted cladogram, Incisivosaurus was identified as the sister taxon to Protarchaeopteryx, together forming the most primitive oviraptorosaurians.
facts.quote: In the unweight cladogram, Incisivosaurus was rendered as the sister taxon to Protarchaeopteryx, with their group being the most primitive oviraptorosaurians.

facts.statement: Incisivosaurus was a small, probably herbivorous theropod dinosaur from the early Cretaceous Period of what is now China.
facts.quote: Incisivosaurus ("incisor lizard") is a genus of small, probably herbivorous theropod dinosaurs from the early Cretaceous Period of what is now the People's Republic of China.

facts.statement: Two juvenile feathered specimens attributed to Incisivosaurus from 2010 showed long symmetrical vaned feathers on the hands and tails, with the rest of the body covered in downy feathers.
facts.quote: In 2010, two feathered oviraptorosaur specimens were described, both of which preserved feather traces. These specimens (both juveniles, though one closer to maturity than the other) showed that the feathers were similar to the related Caudipteryx, with long (symmetrical) vaned feathers on the hand and tail, and the rest of the body covered in simpler, downy feathers.

facts.statement: Feather development specialist Richard Prum disputed the interpretation that feather structures changed with age, suggesting instead that the ribbon-like structures represented feathers in the process of moulting.
facts.quote: However, feather development specialist Richard Prum disputed the above interpretation of the feathers in a November 2010 letter to the journal Nature. Prum noted that the apparently ribbon-like structure of the juvenile's feathers were consistent with pennaceous feathers in the midst of moulting.

facts.statement: Xu et al. (2010) rebutted the moulting hypothesis, arguing the evidence was problematic due to the absence of previous-generation feathers and that the structure was too large to be a pin feather.
facts.quote: However, Xu et al. (2010) rebutted that the purported moulting evidence is problematic due to the complete absence of previous-generation feathers, and suggested that the feather is too large to be considered as a "pin feather".

facts.statement: Incisivosaurus lived during the early Cretaceous Period, approximately 128 million years ago in the Barremian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 128 millones de años en el Barremiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The skull of Incisivosaurus averages about 10 centimeters in length and preserves the most complete dentition known for an oviraptorosaurian.
facts.quote: La descripción inicial de Incisivosaurus por Xu et al. demostró que el cráneo, cuyas media era de aproximadamente 10 centímetros de largo, preservaba la más completa dentición conocida para un oviraptorosauriano.

facts.statement: A 2004 study described Incisivosaurus as having a snout longer than half the total skull length, a thin lower jaw with a long fenestra, and distinctive large, flattened front teeth.
facts.quote: Un posterior estudio de Osmolska et al. en 2004 describió las características esqueléticas que distinguen a Incisivosaurus, incluyendo un hocico largo que medía más de la mitad de la longitud total del cráneo, una quijada inferior delgada con una larga fenestra, sus distintivos dientes delanteros, grandes y aplanados.

facts.statement: The total body length of Incisivosaurus is estimated to be less than one meter.
facts.quote: El largo total del cuerpo se estima en menos de un metro.

facts.statement: Analysis found that Incisivosaurus had reduced olfactory lobes and expanded optic lobes similar to those of ornithomimosaurians.
facts.quote: También encontró que Incisivosaurus tenía lóbulos olfatorios reducidos y lóbulos ópticos expandidos similares a los ornitomimosaurios.

facts.statement: The first specimen was discovered in 2002 in the lowest riverbed layer of the Yixian Formation near Sihetun, close to Beipiao in western Liaoning province.
facts.quote: El primer espécimen en ser descrito por Xu et al. en 2002 fue recogido en el lecho fluvial, la posición más inferior, de la Formación Yixian en el área de Sihetun, cerca de Beipiao, en el oeste de la provincia de Liaoning.

facts.statement: The species was named for its prominent front teeth resembling those of rodents, showing wear patterns common in plant-eating dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado por sus prominentes dientes frontales similares a los de los roedores, con patrones de desgaste encontrados comúnmente en dinosaurios comedores de plantas.

facts.statement: The most significant and unusual feature of this dinosaur is its apparent adaptation to a herbivorous or omnivorous lifestyle.
facts.quote: Lo más significante, y altamente inusual característica de este dinosaurio es su aparente adaptación a un estilo de vida herbívora u omnívora.

facts.statement: The species name honors Dr. Jacques Gauthier, a pioneer in phylogeny, a method of classification.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie fue puesto en honor al doctor Jacques Gauthier, un pionero en la filogenia, un método de clasificación.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis placed Incisivosaurus at the base of the oviraptorosaurian group, making it more primitive than Caudipteryx and the Oviraptoridae.
facts.quote: En su análisis cladistico indicó que Incisivosaurus se ubica en la base del grupo de los ovirraptosaurianos, haciéndolo más primitivo que Caudipteryx y los Oviraptoridae.

facts.statement: Despite unique traits, Incisivosaurus shared many features with typical oviraptorosaurs, allowing its classification within that group.
facts.quote: Además de estas características únicas, Incisivosaurus compartió muchos rasgos con oviraptorosaurianos más típicos, permitiendo su clasificación con este grupo.

facts.statement: In a weighted cladogram, Incisivosaurus became the sister taxon to Protarchaeopteryx, representing the most primitive group of oviraptorosaurs.
facts.quote: En el cladograma ponderado, Incisivosaurus se convirtió en el taxón hermano de Protarchaeopteryx, siendo su grupo los oviraptorosaurios más primitivos.

facts.statement: However, in both weighted analyses, Protarchaeopteryx was the most primitive oviraptorosaurian, with Incisivosaurus as the next most basal.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en ambos análisis ponderados, Protarchaeopteryx fue el oviraptorosauriano más primitivo, con Incisivosaurus como el siguiente más basal.

facts.statement: Incisivosaurus lived from the Barremian to the Albian stages, between 125.77 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Albian (125.77 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is assumed that Incisivosaurus had feathers like other maniraptorans and may have secondarily lost the ability to fly.
facts.quote: De Incisivosaurus se asume que tenía plumas como otros maniraptores y que pudo haber perdido la capacidad de vuelo secundariamente.

facts.statement: It is possible that Incisivosaurus is a synonym of Protarchaeopteryx, though more fossil specimens are needed before the two can be directly compared.
facts.quote: Es posible que Incisivosaurus sea sinónimo de Protarchaeopteryx, aunque más especímenes fósiles son necesarios antes de que los dos puedan ser comparados directamente.

facts.statement: In the third episode of the ITV series Prehistoric Park, it is theorized that Incisivosaurus used its feathered wings for display and that they would have been used for flight in the past.
facts.quote: Incisivosaurus aparece en el tercer episodio de la serie de documentales de ITV Prehistoric Park, donde se teoriza que Incisivosaurus usaba sus "alas con plumas" para exhibición y que habrían sido usadas para volar en el pasado.
